subject: general
question: A cylinder having radius of 5 cm and a height of 10 cm. Find its volume. (π = 3.14)
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Volume** of **cylinder** = π × r² × h

Given: **radius** (r) = 5 cm, **height** (h) = 10 cm, **π** = 3.14

**Volume** = 3.14 × 5² × 10

**Volume** = 3.14 × 25 × 10 = 785 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 785 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius** (r) = 5 cm

**Height** (h) = 10 cm

**π** = 3.14

**Formula Used:**

**Volume** of **Cylinder** = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d71b46bc02a9dd69f4454e778035dbe7d4217400aaae1ffcda2c6345ebf748f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Volume** = 3.14 × (5)² × 10

⇒ **Volume** = 3.14 × 25 × 10

⇒ **Volume** = 78.5 × 10

⇒ **Volume** = 785 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 785 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cylinder

The area of the side surface of the **cylinder** is given by 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The sum of the **CSA** and the areas of the two circular bases: 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same **radius** and **height** as a **cylinder** has exactly one-third of its **volume**: (1/3)πr²h.</p
